extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations (undergraduate/graduate students, early- and mid-career PR professionals, and managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles, roles, and required competencies for effective public relations practice, as presented in a foundational public relations textbook chapter. Covers core axioms for practice, practitioner roles, common work assignments, and professional expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations takes a broad view of an organization’s environment
rubrics_metrics.description: PR attends to a wide range of issues and relationships with stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should monitor and consider many external and internal factors (issues, publics, political climate, media coverage) affecting the organization rather than a narrow marketing-only focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations is part of strategic management
rubrics_metrics.description: PR seeks to avoid or solve problems through a goal-directed process and is integrated with organizational strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR should be involved in management decision-making and problem solving, not treated as an after-the-fact communication function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations outcomes must be quantified and measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes require measurement; practitioners need a detailed understanding and assessment of current conditions and desired future states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement and analytics are essential—define metrics tied to objectives, assess baseline conditions, and quantify changes toward the desired state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning begins with situation diagnosis and objective setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify current conditions motivating the process, contributing forces and actors, objectives for each target public, and the overall program goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning must document situational analysis, stakeholders/actors, specific objectives per target public, and align those objectives with an overarching program goal before tactics are chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations programs must outline the path from current to desired state
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should explain how the organization will get from where it is to where it wants to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include strategies and tactics that logically connect situation analysis and objectives to implementation steps and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations initiatives must have senior management support
rubrics_metrics.description: PR efforts require cooperation and endorsement from top management and cannot be isolated from other operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR practitioners should secure executive buy-in and integrate programs with other organizational units to ensure resources, access, and coordinated action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success depends more on deeds than on words (coordinated deeds and words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational actions tend to determine success or failure more than communication alone; communication must be coordinated with what the organization does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR programs should align messages with authentic organizational behavior; communication can become the problem if actions contradict messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions, communication, and outcomes must be ethical, legal, and socially responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: PR success requires that all activities conform to ethical and legal standards and reflect organizational social responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics and legality are core constraints; programs should be evaluated against ethical norms and the organization's broader social obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate measure of success: organizational impact on society and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Success is ultimately based on the organization's impact on society and culture and on the character/professional careers of the practitioners who implement programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PR programs not only by immediate outputs but by longer-term societal effects and professional integrity of those involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing news releases, feature stories, newsletters, correspondence, website and online content, speeches, reports, scripts, brochures, advertisements, and collateral materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing is the primary entry requirement and remains central throughout a PR career; practitioners must produce clear, accurate, audience-appropriate copy across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting news media and trade publications to secure coverage; responding to media requests; managing social media activities as part of media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and maintain media contacts, craft pitches, respond promptly to verification/information requests, and integrate social media into traditional media strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Gathering information about public opinion, trends, emerging issues, legislation, media coverage, and stakeholder concerns; designing program research and surveys; using online and government databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research to inform situation analysis, objective setting, message development, and evaluation; outsource to research firms when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of clients and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing client relationships, managing expectations, assessing resource allocation, planning logistics, and administering personnel, budgets, and schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective PR practice requires project management skills, clear client/stakeholder communication, realistic scope/resource planning, and personnel administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning (practitioner competency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming and planning in collaboration with other managers: determining needs, establishing priorities, defining publics, setting goals/objectives, and developing messages, strategies, and tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must be able to design integrated programs that link research, objectives, strategies, tactics, and evaluation, and coordinate with other managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling
rubrics_metrics.description: Advising top management on social, political, and regulatory environments; consulting on crisis avoidance/response and devising strategies for critical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR practitioners should provide timely, evidence-based counsel to decision-makers and help shape organizational responses to sensitive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special events
rubrics_metrics.description: Arranging and managing news conferences, runs, conventions, open houses, ribbon cuttings, anniversaries, fund-raisers, visiting dignitaries, contests, award programs, and other observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event planning must align with strategic objectives, manage logistics, media opportunities, and stakeholder experiences to reinforce desired messages and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearances before groups, coaching others for speaking assignments, and managing a speakers’ bureau to provide platforms for the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare spokespeople, tailor presentations to audiences, and use speaking engagements strategically to advance organizational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating communication collateral using multimedia skills: art, typography, photography, layout, desktop publishing, audio/video recording and editing, and audiovisual presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure production quality supports credibility; integrate visual and multimedia elements to reinforce messaging and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing executives and spokespersons for media, instructing others to improve writing and communication skills, and helping introduce changes in organizational culture, policy, structure, and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver practical training that builds internal communication capacity and ensures consistent messaging and behavior across the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal contacts / liaison
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving as liaison with media, community, and other internal/external groups; communicating, negotiating, and managing conflict; building strategic alliances and interpersonal relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship-building and interpersonal skills are essential; maintaining ongoing contacts and alliances supports long-term organizational objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top management responsibility for relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization’s relationships are the responsibility of top management; PR must be embraced at the top and become part of organizational culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR should be positioned as a management function with executive ownership; practitioners must work to embed relationship-building values into organizational culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing as the primary requirement for entry and success
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is identified as the primary requirement for entry to the field and for career success in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students and entry-level practitioners should focus on developing strong writing and editing skills; daily practice and supervision (e.g., editing interns' pitches) are common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media experience is valued by employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers often value journalistic or media experience (even college media) because it provides understanding of media gatekeepers’ values and ways of working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Job candidates should seek media experience to improve employability and effectiveness in media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized education/experience increases employability for technical fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers seek specialized preparation or backgrounds (computer technology, corporate finance, health care, agriculture) for difficult-to-fill positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining PR education with a relevant minor or experience (e.g., health administration, computer science) gives candidates a competitive advantage in specialized sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional accreditation (APR) correlates with higher compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding the Accredited in Public Relations (APR) credential is associated with higher earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuing professional accreditation can enhance career prospects and compensation; consider accreditation as part of professional development planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR serves public interest and democratic information needs
rubrics_metrics.description: PR increases public knowledge and understanding by promoting expression and debate in the marketplace of ideas and provides voices for alternative points of view, including marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should consider the public interest role of PR—promoting debate, serving democratic information needs, and representing underheard constituencies—as part of ethical practice.
